decisions.reason: The distributed airfield lighting control unit is core to the firm's airfield guidance offering, has had substantial R&D investment and a dedicated web page, and fits squarely with the announced move toward integrated, intelligent airport operations.

The air situation display supports the tower and surveillance part of the integrated portfolio, and the firm's visible commitment and investment favour persisting with it despite pandemic-related weakness in airport demand.
The airport systems training program is a low-cost service tied to the installed base and lifecycle support, and any weak uptake can be attributed to temporary COVID travel restrictions.

The airfield ground lighting training course was only mentioned on the website and is less visible, but it is cheap to maintain and complements the firm's core lighting business, so management would attribute low demand to the pandemic.

The collaboration software tool embodies the announced strategic direction of collaborative decision-making and real-time information sharing, so the firm's public and strategic commitment makes dropping it unlikely.

The multilateration surveillance system is a high-investment, long-sales-cycle product central to airfield and tower surveillance, and delayed airport projects can be blamed on the temporary aviation downturn.
